data.title: Hyperliquid whales stack Bitcoin shorts to highest level since October 2025
data.description:
The biggest traders on Hyperliquid are betting against Bitcoin, and they are doing it with conviction.

Whale accounts on the decentralized perpetual futures exchange have pushed their Bitcoin short positions to the highest level since October 2025. These are some of the largest leveraged accounts in on-chain trading, and right now most of their money is leaning one way.

As of November 7, 2026, Hyperliquid whales hold between $892 million and $924 million in Bitcoin shorts. On the other side of the ledger, their longs total between $454 million and $483 million.

That puts whale shorts at nearly double whale longs. The resulting net short bias is estimated at between $345 million and $470 million, depending on the snapshot used.

The largest single whale short is approximately $178.5 million, opened at an entry price around $76,390. Other notable shorts on the platform include positions of $155 million and $101.8 million, plus several more exceeding $60 million each.

Bitcoin was trading around $75,800 to $76,000 at the time of the data.

Hyperliquid whales flipped to a net short position on October 27, 2026, and have been adding to that stance since.

Total Bitcoin perpetual open interest on Hyperliquid sits at roughly $3.13 billion. Whale positioning represents a sizable slice of that pool.

Hyperliquid runs on its own Layer-1 blockchain and has become one of the more closely watched venues for leveraged crypto trading. Because large positions there are visible, traders across the market tend to treat whale moves on the exchange as a sentiment gauge.

The bearish lean is not limited to Bitcoin. Some of the same significant whale accounts are also shorting HYPE, Hyperliquid's native token.

The straightforward read is that the platform's largest players expect Bitcoin to fall in the near term. A net short bias of this size points to prevailing bearish sentiment among well-capitalized traders.

Heavy short interest concentrated around current price levels creates the conditions for a short squeeze. If Bitcoin climbs instead of falling, short sellers face mounting losses. Some may be forced to close their positions, and closing a short means buying the asset back.

The entry prices matter here. The largest whale opened its short around $76,390, just above where Bitcoin has been trading. Sustained moves above the entry levels of the biggest shorts would put real pressure on those accounts.

For traders watching from the sidelines, a few markers deserve attention. The first is whether the net short bias keeps growing or starts to unwind. The second is Bitcoin's behavior around the $76,000 area, where the largest short entries cluster. The third is the HYPE shorts. If bearish bets on the exchange's own token continue to build alongside the Bitcoin positions, it would reinforce the picture of broad caution among the platform's biggest players rather than a narrow trade on a single asset.

What the data does make clear is that the largest accounts on one of crypto's most watched derivatives venues have chosen a side. Their positioning has not been this bearish in more than a year.

data.title: Tesla to expand Cybertruck production in bid to fill orders before dismantling line next year
data.description:
Tesla will add an extra production shift to try to complete outstanding Cybertruck orders before dismantling the line next year for a planned expansion of Cybercab production, CEO Elon Musk said on Saturday.

"The Cybertruck order backlog is currently far more than Tesla can make before dismantling the line for Cybercab expansion around June/July next year," Musk said in a post on X.

data.title: Nvidia CEO was romantically involved with alleged Chinese spy, U.S. memo says: FT
data.description:
The Trump administration believes Nvidia’s CEO, Jensen Huang, had a romantic relationship with a Chinese woman who allegedly served China’s main intelligence agency as a spy, The Financial Times reported on Saturday, citing a government memo.

Based on information obtained by American intelligence, U.S. officials wrote the memo earlier this year stating that Huang had been romantically involved with Alice Huang, an executive at a Singapore-based client of the chipmaker, according to people familiar with the matter.

U.S. intelligence officials think that China’s Ministry of State Security intelligence agency hired Alice Huang as a spy, the people added. She served as an executive at Megaspeed, a company facing U.S. scrutiny over allegations that it smuggled advanced Nvidia chips into China, violating U.S. export controls.

The memo was shared with a select group of high-ranking Trump administration officials shortly before President Donald Trump travelled to Beijing for a summit with his Chinese counterpart, Xi Jinping in May.

The White House and CIA declined to comment on FT’s requests for comment. Nvidia also declined to comment. The company, the world’s second largest in terms of market capitalization, has previously said its CEO meets “thousands of customer executives every year.”

The news of the memo came days after three House Republican committee leaders sent a letter to Nvidia CEO asking him to attend a closed-door briefing regarding reports on his alleged relationship with Alice Huang.

“Recent reports raise significant national security concerns regarding the PRC's access to sensitive U.S. technology and information," the GOP lawmakers wrote in the letter sent on Wednesday.

data.title: Binance CFO Kaiser Ng steps down, Justin Yek named new finance chief
data.description:
Binance's finance chief Kaiser Ng is leaving the company to pursue another venture, the world's biggest cryptocurrency exchange said days after hackers stole $6.3 billion from the platform in a record heist.

"Kaiser Ng has decided to pursue a new venture after more than five years at Binance, with a transition plan implemented over the last half year," Binance Co-Chief Executive Officer Yi He said in a statement on Saturday.

Justin Yek, a longtime finance executive who was most recently vice-president of finance at Airwallex, is taking over as CFO.

The announcement comes just over a week after Binance said hackers stole cryptocurrency in a sophisticated attack that began months earlier with the compromise of several employees' computers.

Binance has said the breach, which unfolded on October 29, started with malware hidden in software downloads and fake job recruitment efforts targeting engineers. It said it will fully reimburse affected customers.

The FBI has blamed a North Korean hacking group for the theft, an allegation Pyongyang has denied.

Ng has been CFO at Binance since January 2022 and has previously worked at rival crypto exchange Kraken, according to his LinkedIn profile.

data.title: Rs.90 dividend per share: This stock announces 900% payout - Do you own? Payment, record date, returns
data.description:
New Delhi, Nov. 7 -- Shares of Bayer CropScience Limited will remain in focus next week due to the upcoming record date for its Rs.90 per equity share dividend payout. The company also announced its second quarter result for the financial year 2026-27.

Bayer CropScience Limited share price closed 0.45% higher on Friday, after seeing 1.64% jump over the last five trading sessions.

The company's board of directors, on Tuesday, November 3, announced an interim dividend of Rs.90 per equity share with a face value of Rs.10 each (ie 900% of the face value) for FY27. The board has also fixed record date to determine the eligibility of shareholders for the payout.

The board fixed Thursday, November 12, as the record date to determine the eligibility of shareholders for the payout. Which means that investors must own the stock before the record date to qualify for the payout.

As per the company's BSE filing, the board will disburse the dividend payout among investors by Monday, November 30, 2026.

Alongside announcement of dividend, the company also reported a net profit of Rs.166.2 crore in the second quarter of FY27, against Rs.152.7 crore reported in the year ago period. Its net profit before tax (PBT) increased by 6% to Rs.211.4 crore during the quarter under review.

The stock closed 0.45% higher at Rs.3316.50 per share on BSE with a market capitalisation of Rs.14,905.04 crore on Friday. The stock has surged 1.64% in one week, but has declined 6.17% in one month, 21.32% in three months and around 30.29% in one year.

data.title: Solana’s October Upgrade Review Puts 200ms Slots and $5B in Tokenized Assets in Focus
data.description:
TL;DR: Solana Foundation’s November 6 ecosystem review says two protocol changes went live in October: a reduction in target slot time to 200 milliseconds and Alpenglow consensus activation. It also reports a record $5 billion in real-world asset value. These are different metrics, and none alone proves a better experience for every application.

After a month filled with announcements, Solana has published a consolidated account of what changed on its network. The Foundation’s October 2026 ecosystem roundup, released November 6, links a pair of major performance upgrades with increased tokenized-asset activity and a growing roster of payment integrations.

The review is useful because it separates infrastructure that has activated from applications and partnerships still seeking wider use. It also offers a chance to examine how technical speed claims translate into financial operations.

Two protocol changes, two different measures

According to the Foundation, a final stage of SIMD-0525 activated on October 9, reducing target slot times from the original 400 milliseconds to 200 milliseconds. Shorter slots aim to reduce the interval at which network leaders produce blocks. They do not guarantee that every transaction is confirmed within 200 milliseconds under all network conditions.

A second change followed on October 21 when Alpenglow replaced TowerBFT consensus on mainnet. The protocol targets roughly 150-millisecond finality. Finality describes when a transaction is sufficiently settled according to the network’s rules, and should not be confused with transaction submission, application response time or a merchant receiving funds in a bank account.

NewsBTC covered the Alpenglow activation earlier in the autumn. The new roundup does not make it a second launch. It provides a broader, dated view of how the two changes fit together, while reminding readers that production reliability has to be measured over time.

Tokenized assets grow beyond trading demonstrations

The Foundation reports that real-world assets on Solana reached $5 billion in value during October, alongside approximately $60 billion in decentralized-exchange trading volume and 14 million addresses holding stablecoins. These numbers measure different things. Asset value is not trading volume; a blockchain address is not necessarily a person; and gross turnover is not revenue to applications or validators.

The review includes new or expanded connections to traditional finance. J.P. Morgan Asset Management brought tokenized money market funds to the network through Morgan Money. The Foundation also describes stock-related products from Securitize and investment portfolios from Ondo, subject to their own eligibility conditions. For institutional users, the question is not only whether a token can move quickly but whether its legal ownership, redemption rights and custody arrangements remain clear.

That is also the theme behind Solana’s delivery-versus-payment programme, which seeks to coordinate an asset and its payment in one settlement process. Better throughput can help, but it cannot replace legal and operational safeguards.

A broader payments test is beginning

The Foundation’s update lists stablecoin and remittance activity involving Samsung Wallet, Fiserv and Western Union, as well as integrations with business-payment services. Some products have launched, while other announcements refer to planned support, geographically limited access or commercial pilots. Those distinctions should survive any headline about ‘mainstream adoption’.

For developers and validators, the next meaningful evidence is sustained uptime, consistent finality under load, integration reliability and the cost of operating infrastructure. For investors, it is whether tokenized value corresponds to assets customers can actually redeem and use. Solana’s October was busy by the Foundation’s account; November’s challenge is showing the upgrades make routine financial activity more dependable, not merely more impressive on paper.

This article was written by the News Desk and edited by Samuel Rae.

data.title: New Zealand vote leaves National, Labour nearly deadlocked
data.description:
By Lucy Craymer and Alasdair Pal

New Zealanders were unlikely to have much clarity on Sunday over who will govern the country for the next three years, after overnight results showed the ruling centre-right National Party and main opposition Labour Party were nearly deadlocked in the popular vote.

Electoral Commission preliminary results showed that both parties were polling at just under 30% of the popular vote, with only a few hundred votes separating them.

An Electoral Commission projection showed the current three-party ruling coalition, led by National, would secure a two-seat majority after an election dominated by a struggling economy and voter disillusionment with the two largest parties.

The final vote count, however, which will include special votes that have historically favoured left-leaning parties, will not be released until November 27.

Until then the incumbent coalition, led by Prime Minister Christopher Luxon, will continue to operate as a caretaker government.

If the National-led coalition loses its majority at the official count, either it or a left-leaning coalition would require the support of the centrist Opportunity Party, which looks likely to enter parliament for the first time.

Luxon has repeatedly ruled out working with Opportunity, but Mona Krewel, a senior political science lecturer at Victoria University of Wellington, said it was possible the two parties could still work together.

"I actually would take them for very centrist, very pragmatic, and so I do think they could make it work with National," she said.

The country switched to a mixed member proportional system in 1996, meaning people vote for both a party and a local constituency candidate. There are 71 constituency, or "electorate", seats and at least 49 party list seats.

However, National and a minor party, Te Pati Maori, each won a disproportionately high share of constituency seats relative to their popular-vote support due to tactical voting, reshaping the balance of seats in parliament and sparking debate about the electoral system.

"It certainly looks as if we're on track for the least proportional parliament that we've had, as a result of the vagaries of the rules around how electorate seats interact with the parliament as a whole," political commentator Ben Thomas said.

data.title: How One Winery Is Fighting an Industry Slump — WSJ
data.description:
By Elizabeth Garone

This isn't a great time to own a vineyard.

The wine industry is in the midst of a major downturn, with some growers tearing up healthy vineyards to plant higher-yielding crops, while others are declaring bankruptcy.

California, which produces more than 80% of the wine grapes in the U.S., is feeling the hit especially hard. In 2025, California's growers crushed a total of 2.76 million tons of grapes — down about 6.1% from the 2024 crush of 2.94 million tons. It was the lowest total in more than 20 years, according to a report by the Pacific Regional Office of the USDA National Agricultural Statistics Service and the California Department of Food and Agriculture.

A number of factors are slamming the industry, including public-health warnings about the dangers of alcohol and changing consumer tastes, especially among younger drinkers. High tariffs aren't helping: Last year, for instance, U.S. wine exports to Canada fell by 78% from 2024.

To weather the downturn, wineries in California and across the country are coming up with new strategies. They are focusing on higher-end wines — which haven't been hit as hard by the drop — as well as trying to come up with innovative products and services to supplement wine sales.

To get a closer look at the pressures on wineries, and what they are doing to survive, consider Somerset Vineyard & Winery, in Temecula, Calif., located in the Inland Empire between Los Angeles and San Diego. In 2025, Somerset's revenue dropped to about $3.3 million from $3.5 million in 2024, and the winery posted its first net loss.

"When I bought the winery, I thought it would be so much fun if we could sit behind a bar and say, 'Would you like a red or a white?' " says co-owner Kurt Tiedt. "I thought that was how easy it might be, but no, it's very, very challenging."

House of the spirits

Back in 2018, Tiedt, his wife, Nesreen, and a handful of childhood friends purchased the closed Keyways Vineyard & Winery and renamed it Somerset, after the street they grew up on. Its vineyards were in excellent condition, Tiedt says, and the new owners still grow the four varieties that Keyways had in place: Tempranillo, Grenache, Viognier and Roussanne.

Wine represents the biggest chunk of Somerset's revenue. In 2025, the winery's tasting room accounted for nearly two-thirds of total sales, $1.9 million. (That tasting-room figure includes wine — and other merchandise — bought by people who visit Somerset on wine tours.) Wine-club sales add almost another third of total revenue — about $1 million — but membership has fallen to around 2,100 or 2,200, versus a peak of 2,600 during the pandemic. The rest of revenue — about $400,000 total — comes from other parts of the business, such as special events and rental fees for a house on-site.

Somerset now produces roughly 100,000 bottles of wine a year but only grows about a quarter of the grapes it uses, buying the rest from several local vineyards — an arrangement that lets Somerset make up to 15 to 18 different wines in any given year. The owners have also bought a second, larger winery nearby, and are looking to grow varieties that other vineyards aren't offering. Their focus is on grapes that thrive in the climate, which mirrors the Spanish Mediterranean and the Rhone Valley of France.

"Temecula typically has hot summer days and pleasant summer evenings due to the ocean breeze," Tiedt says. "It is great for grapes."

The winery currently has more than 160,000 finished bottles in its cellars, Tiedt says — representing about $6.4 million in retail sales, at an average of $40 per bottle. Along with other wines currently being aged, Somerset has three years of inventory in reserve. About 100,000 bottles of that stock are red wines, which Somerset prefers to age for 18 to 24 months or more, versus just three to six for white varieties.

Newly planted vines need about three years before they can be harvested, and the winery tends to sign medium-term deals, three to five years, with the vineyards where it buys grapes.

Some deals only run a single season, however — and recently, many of those short-term agreements are for white-wine grapes. Customer demand for white wines soared this year, thanks to an unusually hot summer, among other factors; chilled white wines are better suited to the weather than reds.

"We have increased our white-wine production by 300% this year and lowered our red-wine production," Tiedt says.

Aiming high

Like a lot of other wineries, Somerset is betting heavily on higher-priced wines, which it sells largely to wine-club members. Its top-selling white varieties run about $34 a bottle, well above industry average, against a production cost of about $10, for a hefty 71% margin. But Tiedt stresses that the production cost doesn't include insurance, maintenance and other significant overhead, which cut down the profit.

The most expensive wines — those made in special terracotta vessels — run about $100, but cost more to produce, between $15 to $20 a bottle. That is a margin of up to 85%, but once again, Tiedt points out that the production cost doesn't include overhead, such as the long-term investment in the terracotta vessels.

Over the past couple of years, a number of big expenses have driven up those overhead costs. For one, there are high expenses from building a new kitchen — $800,000 — and making other improvements. Another big pain point: a one-time surge in annual fire and liability insurance, to $205,000 from $65,000, because of the fire losses from Napa Valley and Los Angeles. "That policy cost dropped to $140,000 this year, but we are still paying for the fires in other markets," Tiedt says.

All those costs took a toll on the bottom line. In 2025, Somerset posted a loss of about $90,000, down from a profit of $12,000 the year before and $211,000 in 2023.

Spreading the vines

For smaller wineries to be successful in the current market, they need to be doing at least one of three things, says Christian Miller, the director of research for nonprofit market-research firm Wine Market Council. They need to sell to a less-tapped consumer niche; offer a distinctive wine (or other product); and/or be more efficient with things like hospitality and customer relations.

"A certain amount of growth has to be supported by making your winery's visitation experience more attractive than others, as well as increasing awareness and interest," says Miller.

Indeed, tours are crucial for Somerset. The winery gets fees from the tour companies for each visit, about $327,000 last year, but those fees basically just cover the cost of holding tastings for the visitors and giving them tours. On top of the fees, though, guests also spend an average of $14 on wine and merchandise, such as candles made using the winery's bottles and T-shirts with its history. (The shirts are one of the most popular items, Tiedt says, and they make for great advertising.) Last year, those sales to tourists hit $790,000, which the winery counts as part of the $1.9 million revenue total for its tasting room.

Many guests also end up becoming repeat customers or joining a wine club, says Tiedt.

Of course, tours can also bring headaches. "It is very difficult when other wineries overpour their guests at the stop before our winery and we have to deal with tipsy or even drunk guests," says Tiedt.

He has learned how to handle these guests delicately, and with humor. "An angry drunk person kicked out of a tour is a good way to get a bad Yelp review," he says.

In addition to tours, the winery's owners are pitching the place as a local gathering spot — with concerts and open-mic nights — and a venue for events such as weddings and corporate conferences. They stay open late some nights with food service, to lure in customers who don't want to visit during the hot afternoon hours.

The expanded hours "brought a lot of people in and also got us a lot of loyal wine-club members," Tiedt says.

Another source of income: an eight-bedroom house on the property. Rental income for the house, usually booked by the day or week, runs $200,000 annually, with up to another $100,000 for events such as weddings. A recent full-day rental of the winery by a corporation brought in $50,000. Profit from this side of the business usually runs about $20,000 to $30,000, but it didn't turn one last year, due to extensive and costly renovations.

Tiedt isn't too worried about Somerset's future even with the challenges in the industry. In his prior career in real estate, he learned the up and down cycles of that industry, he says. "The wine industry also has its up and down cycles, and I believe we are positioned well for this downturn."

Write to reports@wsj.com.

data.title: French presidential hopeful Melenchon pledges economic stimulus, renews NATO exit call
data.description:
Key points:
  • "We have no business being in NATO," Melenchon says
  • Pledges to freeze prices and link wages to inflation
  • Seeks higher taxes on the wealthy, scrapping of the capital income flat tax

By Petra Wischgoll

Jean-Luc Melenchon criticised NATO and "American wars" while pledging an economic stimulus-led revival on Saturday as he unveiled his 2027 presidential programme at a rally in the northern Paris suburb of Le Bourget.

Setting out his economic programme, Melenchon said his anti-capitalist France Unbowed (LFI) party would do the opposite to President Emmanuel Macron.

"We are going to do exactly the opposite — that is to say, a policy of stimulus," he told some 17,000 supporters, according to campaign director Manuel Bompard.

"First, through consumer spending, because in our country that accounts for more than half of economic activity. And secondly, through billions (of euros) that already exist. They are savings that must be channelled towards our country's ecological and social needs."

Melenchon, 75, is viewed as the strongest contender on the left, and recent opinion polls have shown him reaching the presidential runoff next April against Marine Le Pen of the far right. But they also indicate he would lose in the second round.

His manifesto, titled "L'Avenir en commun" ("A Shared Future"), is the fifth edition of LFI's programme and largely reaffirms policies that have underpinned Melenchon's previous presidential bids.

Among the programme's flagship pledges is to repeal Macron's pension overhaul, which gradually raised France's minimum retirement age from 62 to 64 in an effort to shore up public finances. LFI says it would restore retirement at 60 for people who have contributed to the system for 40 years.

Melenchon said an immediate response to the cost-of-living crisis should include measures to "freeze prices, raise the minimum wage, index wages to inflation."

LFI's programme calls for increasing the net monthly minimum wage to €1,700 ($1,890) from around €1,480, abolishing the flat tax on capital income, raising taxes on the wealthiest households and capping prices for essential foods.

On foreign policy, Melenchon's programme reiterates his long-standing criticism of NATO and calls for France's gradual withdrawal from the alliance, beginning with an exit from its integrated military command.

"We have no business being in NATO, nor in American wars," Melenchon said. "France must build a global front of non-aligned countries."

Melenchon's programme also reiterates his support for a gradual phase-out of nuclear power in favour of a fully renewable electricity system, including scrapping the planned EPR2 programme of the planned new generation of state-backed nuclear reactors and not extending the lifespan of nuclear plants beyond 60 years.

It also criticises German influence on EU economic policy, describing Berlin as Europe's chief defender of "ordoliberalism", an economic philosophy centred on strict budget rules, price stability and independent monetary policy.

($1 = 0.8974 euros)

data.title: Bulls vs. Bears: NVIDIA sparks valuation debate as stock nears six-month low
data.description:
Nvidia recorded its sixth consecutive weekly drop this week amid a broader selloff in the U.S. tech sector, adding to the sharp losses the company recorded in October, which also happened to be its worst monthly decline for this year. With its share price approaching levels not seen since April, Seeking Alpha analysts reviewed their positions on the stock, triggering a healthy conversation around its valuation.

The Bulls

“Nvidia Corporation is a Strong Buy after a 20% selloff, with current sentiment-driven declines presenting a compelling entry point,” wrote SA analyst Oliver Rodzianko in “Here's Why I Bought Nvidia While The Market Cried In Fear (Rating Upgrade).” Even under conservative growth assumptions, NVDA's fair value ranges from $156 to $252 per share, offering significant upside versus current levels.

“NVDA stock trades at just over 13x FY28 EPS targets, not reflecting sustainable growth prospects fueled by SpaceX's commitments,” noted Seeking Alpha Investing Group Leader Stone Fox Capital in “Nvidia: SpaceX Offers An Ignored Bonus.” “Nvidia Corporation is set up to get a large bonus via SpaceX's massive AI data center plans, providing a significant growth catalyst.”

“NVDA's 70% projected revenue growth and 74% gross margins are underpinned by robust AI demand and supply constraints, not demand limitations.,” added Index Analyst in “Nvidia: Competitive Moat Widening; Buy.” “At $301.53 per share of valuation, there's a possible upside of 46% from the current share price of $206.”

“The selloff on Oct. 30 was triggered by something other than Nvidia,” argued SA analyst Benjamin C. Barry in “Nvidia: Trade The Fear With NVDL.” “That means the poor performance from Intel and nervousness in the credit markets wiped about $220 billion from Nvidia's valuation, despite the fact that Nvidia had just raised its own outlook.”

“Nvidia’s biggest problem right now is that customers want more than it can make, and frankly, that’s a good problem to have,” wrote Rick Orford in “Nvidia May Actually Raise Its 70% Growth Guide In November.” “The stock also costs less today than when I last talked about it, and I’m comfortable with that setup as long as the second answer doesn’t turn ugly.”

The Bears

“NVDA trades at a 17.7x 1-yr fwd P/E, below semiconductor peers and its historical average, creating a valuation counterweight,” opined SA analyst Hunting Alphas in “Nvidia: Time To Lock In The Profits.” “Vera Rubin adoption and rising B200 rental rates support Nvidia’s growth outlook, creating upside risks despite pressure on margins and cash conversion.”

“My valuation model implies NVDA is overvalued by 11%, with significant downside if financing constraints and competitive pressures persist into FY28,” wrote Bears of Wall Street in “Nvidia: Brace For The Worst.” “We believe that the bearish thesis has only strengthened, and Nvidia’s stock has plenty of room to fall.”

“Despite the CDS widening by 80 bps since July, NVDA's share price has risen 12%, highlighting a stark disconnect between credit and equity markets,” argued Stuart Allsopp in “Nvidia: Equity Investors Are Ignoring The Surge In Implied Default Risk.” “To justify an equity position, NVDA must deliver at least a 6.7% annual return for 30 years, requiring sustained free cash flow growth and sustained multiples.”

“On paper, Nvidia is cheaper on a growth-adjusted basis than it has been for most of the past five years,” wrote The Techie in “Nvidia: Jensen Can't Spend His Way Out Of This One.” “However, that multiple only holds if the growth estimates hold, and custom silicon, China share loss, and stressed neocloud customers are precisely the risks to those estimates.”

data.title: Q2 results race: Samvardhana Motherson vs Uno Minda - Which auto ancillary stock scores better? Revenue, profit, target
data.description:
New Delhi, Nov. 7 -- Samvardhana Motherson vs Uno Minda: Two of the most widely tracked auto ancillary firms, Uno Minda and Samvardhana Motherson International recently announced their second quarter results for the financial year 2026-27. While Samvardhana Motherson reported 42% year-on-year jump in its Q2 profit, later reported 36.6% annual jump in profit.

Here is a detailed comparison of the Q2 results of the two companies for FY27, along with their target price post result announcement.

Samvardhana Motherson's net profit increased by 42% on an annual basis to Rs.1,175.32 crore, on strong revenue growth. Its net profit stood at Rs.827 crore during the year-ago period. Uno Minda's net profit stood at Rs.440.81 crore in Q2FY27, up 36.6% from Rs.322.79 crore reported in the year-ago period.

Samvardhana's total revenue from operations surged to Rs.38,279.85 crore, from Rs.30,172.97 crore last fiscal, during the second quarter under review, on a year-on-year basis. Uno Minda's net revenue increased by 38.2% to Rs.6,655.42 crore in the September quarter, up from Rs.4,814.03 crore in the year-ago period.

data.title: Egypt reopens embassy in Libya's Tripoli after 12-year closure
data.description:
Egypt reopened its embassy in Libya's capital Tripoli on Saturday after a 12-year absence, marking a rapprochement with the country's western-based administration, the foreign affairs ministry in Cairo said in a statement.

  • The move marks a shift for Cairo, which has been one of the most prominent backers of eastern-based military commander Khalifa Haftar, a rival of the Tripoli-based government

  • Egypt closed its Tripoli embassy in 2014, when many foreign missions there closed amid an escalating conflict that saw rival governments set themselves up in the capital and in the east of the huge North African country

  • Egypt's foreign affairs minister Badr Abdelatty was quoted in the statement as saying at the reopening ceremony that the historical significance of the embassy building "aligns with the deep-rooted human and cultural ties that characterize Egyptian-Libyan relations"

  • Oil producer Libya has been plunged into chaos since the fall of Muammar Gaddafi in a NATO-backed uprising in 2011

  • In Benghazi in eastern Libya there is the Libyan National Army under military commander Khalifa Haftar and the House of Representatives, and a government led by Osama Hammad. In the west there is the internationally recognised Government of National Unity headed by PM Abdulhamid Dbeibah and the High Council of State in Tripoli

data.title: Slop Cash, From elizaOS Creator Shaw Walters, Opens Public Bidding on Umia After Passing Its $400K Minimum
data.description:
New York, New York, November 7th, 2026, Chainwire

The first project from Umia's Cohort 1 cleared its minimum raise during the early bid, with more than 200 bidders across three access lanes. The public round on Robinhood Chain is open to everyone until 10 November.

Umia, the onchain platform for launching, funding and governing projects, today opened the public round of the auction for Slop Cash at around 15:35 UTC, after early-bid commitments passed the project's $400,000 minimum raise within 12 hours. Slop Cash is built by Shaw Walters, creator of the open-source AI agent framework elizaOS, and Drew Pierson. It is the first Cohort 1 project to reach auction on Umia, following $UMIA, the first token launched through the system in August.

Slop Cash is a non-custodial funding rail for open-source software. Funding projects put up monthly prize pools against their repositories, and contributors, human or AI agent, work on GitHub as usual. Only merged pull requests and accepted code reviews are scored, in public, and funders sign payouts from wallets Slop Cash does not control.

On Umia, the minimum raise is a structural condition which determines if the launch is successful: had commitments fallen short, every bid would have been refunded in full. With it cleared, the token is now set to launch, deploying the onchain liquidity and placing the project’s domains and social accounts in one legal wrapper under the Umia system. Spending beyond a fixed monthly allowance requires a decision market, where the option the markets value highest is executed.

The early bid ran through three lanes, each with its own cap, and no private round came before it. The Slop community path was reserved for contributors, reviewers and maintainers with accepted work on Slop-listed repositories, who proved their GitHub activity through the Umia Extension. The extension generates a zkTLS proof in the participant's browser, confirming eligibility without the account, login or underlying data becoming visible. That lane filled its $200,000 allocation within the first day. The other lanes served UMIA holders through Umia Pass, and whitelisted funds and angels.

has a total supply of 100 million, of which 45% is offered in the auction and 2% goes to Umia's treasury as launch provider. The token directs Slop Cash's own treasury through decision markets and has no say over contributor payouts, scores or whether a pull request is merged.

"Slop Cash is the first outside project to go through the whole Umia system, from the legal wrapper to the auction to the treasury its token will govern. The early bid put the people who ship the work first in line, and the public round now opens the auction to everyone," said Francesco Mosterts, Co-Founder of Umia.

The public round is open at app.umia.finance/p/slop-cash/auction until 10 November. Further Cohort 1 projects are expected to launch in the coming weeks, subject to onboarding and legal review.

About Umia

Umia is a full-stack platform for launching, funding and governing projects onchain. Each project launched through Umia operates within a single legal wrapper, with its intellectual property, operating team and treasury under one structure and board-level decisions delegated to onchain decision markets. Umia is incubated by Chainbound. Learn more at docs.umia.finance.

data.title: Samsung Wallet’s USDC on Solana Is Live — Here’s What the Rollout Actually Covers
data.description:
TL;DR: A Solana Foundation update dated November 5 confirms that Samsung Wallet’s stablecoin account went live on November 2 for eligible US Galaxy owners. USDC transfers and certain international bank payouts are supported, but the headline 82 million compatible devices should not be mistaken for 82 million active users.

A crypto feature that does not feel like a crypto feature may be one of the most consequential ways digital payments reach a wider audience. In a November 5 launch confirmation, the Solana Foundation said Samsung Wallet’s Stablecoin Account became available on November 2. For eligible US Galaxy users, it places USDC inside a familiar wallet app rather than asking them to install and learn a separate cryptocurrency application.

That is a tangible step beyond the launch window described in NewsBTC’s earlier look at Samsung’s planned rollout. But the most useful questions concern what people can do today, who qualifies and what still depends on outside providers.

Transfers without a separate crypto app

The Foundation says eligible users can buy, hold, send and receive USDC over Solana within Samsung Wallet. Bastion provides licensed custody and infrastructure, with Coinbase serving as sub-custodian through Coinbase Prime Vault. That structure matters. Customers see the convenience of a familiar interface, while their assets still depend on a chain of infrastructure and custody providers.

US customers can transfer USDC to other eligible Samsung Wallet users and compatible external wallets. The announcement says Samsung charges no transfer fee for these routes, although other providers may charge fees. A separate path allows eligible users to send funds to qualifying bank accounts in more than 60 countries, potentially arriving as local currency. Available corridors and charges vary by destination; the distinction between a blockchain transfer and a bank payout is important.

The feature sits inside Samsung Wallet’s Quick access area alongside payment cards and everyday credentials. That small interface decision could matter more to adoption than a headline transaction-speed benchmark, because habitual use often depends on how much friction an app removes.

Device reach is not transaction volume

The announcement refers to approximately 82 million compatible Galaxy devices in the United States. That is a ceiling for potential access, not evidence of adoption. It says nothing about the number of activated accounts, transfers completed, average transaction size or users who return the following month.

The eligibility restrictions are also substantial. According to the Foundation, users need to be at least 18, reside in the US, have a Samsung account and use a compatible Galaxy device running Android 13 or later. New York residents are excluded at launch. These requirements make the real reachable population smaller than the device figure.

The payments story extends the institutional work covered in NewsBTC’s report on Solana’s delivery-versus-payment tool, but the two solve different problems. One targets consumer remittances; the other aims at financial-asset settlement.

What success will look like

Samsung has described potential future expansion into online and in-store stablecoin payments and additional markets, subject to regulation. Those ideas are not live features simply because the stablecoin account has launched. Nor should this launch be read as a forecast for SOL’s price: consumer payments can be valuable without creating a predictable relationship between wallet activity and demand for the network token.

A fair assessment will require active-account numbers, real-world fees, payout times, failed-payment handling and whether the feature reduces friction relative to existing remittance services. The verified news is that the service is now operational for a defined group of customers. The commercial test begins after that announcement, when people decide whether to use it again.

This article was written by the News Desk and edited by Samuel Rae.

data.title: Real estate stocks gain as the Blue Wave sends Treasury yields lower
data.description:
Real estate stocks were gaining as the Democrats sweep of Congress in the U.S. midterm elections sent the longer-term Treasury yields down.

Tuesday's midterm results reflected voter frustration over rising prices, the Iran war, and government corruption. The party is positioning itself for an aggressive oversight agenda targeting the Trump administration and powerful special interests.

United States 10-Year Bond Yield hit its lowest level in about two months this week as a collapse in crude oil prices and the midterm elections drained stagflation fears and deficit anxiety, according to a recent report by Investing.com.

Housing-related stocks surged as the elections reignited hopes of several issues plaguing the housing market getting addressed, according to CNBC News.

"Democratic control of Congress raises the potential for lower tariffs, which we estimate represent ~$7,500 of additional cost per home, a de-escalation of the conflict in the Middle East, and a less restrictive approach to immigration policy," UBS reportedly said.

The potential legislations to keep an eye on include the More Homes on the Market Act: a bipartisan bill that would double capital gains exclusions, and the First Home Affordability Act: a 10% first-time homebuyer tax credit, the report noted.

Meanwhile, Wall Street's major indexes went from cheerful optimism after the 2026 midterm elections to experiencing their worst day in over a year and a half. The indexes saw severe weekly losses from an ongoing technology selloff and policy fears related to AI.

Weekly Winners & Losers

Among largecap stocks, American Healthcare REIT led the winners, adding 8.20% to close the week at $57.91. The health care REIT exceeded analyst estimates in terms of third-quarter earnings and revenue.

Iron Mountain (-8.61% W/W to $106.52) topped the decliners despite Q3 earnings surpassing expectations amid a disappointing Q4 guidance.

data.title: Revised prices on anti-cancer medicines effective from Monday, estimated annual savings of over ₹3500 crore
data.description:
The revised prices on 137 anti-cancer drugs will kick in on Monday, bringing annual savings of over ₹3,500 crore, said a note from the National Pharmaceutical Pricing Authority (NPPA).

Drug companies making these medicines were forced to revise prices after the Centre capped trade margins on these drugs at 30 per cent, under the Supreme Court’s watch.

Giving the latest update, the NPPA said on Saturday, about 76 pharmaceutical companies have revised MRPs for 1225 anti-cancer formulations, covering 121 drugs. A reduction has been reported in 1031 formulations of anti-cancer medicines, with 600 brands reporting above 50 per cent reduction, and the highest reduction being 96.45 per cent, the NPPA said.

In fact, it said, about 10-15 drugs (of the 137) were yet to be launched in India, and the Trade Margin Rationalisation (TMR) will be applicable to them when they are brought into the country. According to a source, of 1330 updated prices, about 203 brand prices remain unchanged.

“Every retailer, dealer, hospital and institution is required to prominently display the revised MRP list of anti-cancer medicines on their websites and in their premises,” the NPPA said.

Some of the medicines seeing a reduction in prices included:

# Bevacizumab 100 MG Injection (for Lung, Colon, Ovary and Cervical Cancer) – with Zydus Lifesciences price reducing from ₹ 25,995 to ₹3,318;

# Denosumab 60 MG Injection (for breast and prostate cancer – prevents bone loss) - Reliance Life Sciences – down from ₹ 24,955 to ₹6,240;

data.title: Star Health Settles Over Rs 780 Cr In Cancer Claims In H1 FY27, Women Account For 60%
data.description:
The insurer settles over 85,900 cancer-related claims, highlighting the growing importance of early detection, treatment access and financial protection for women

Star Health and Allied Insurance Company Limited settled more than 85,900 cancer-related claims worth over Rs 780 crore during the first half of FY2026-27, with women accounting for nearly 60 per cent of the payouts, the company announced on 5 November, 2026. Settlements for women increased 17 per cent year-on-year, while nearly 30 per cent of the total claims were associated with people aged between 51 and 60 years.

According to the insurer, more than 45 per cent of the cancer claim payouts originated from Maharashtra, Kerala and Tamil Nadu. The figures highlight the financial support required by patients and families navigating cancer treatment.

A 2013 study published in the Asian Pacific Journal of Cancer Prevention, based on Indian Council of Medical Research (ICMR) National Cancer Registry Programme data from 2001-2004, projected approximately 9.35 lakh new cancer cases among women in India for 2026. Breast and cervical cancers were identified among the leading contributors. The figure represents a projection rather than an observed 2026 count.

Screening And Financial Protection

Government screening initiatives have also expanded. By February 2026, approximately 8.73 crore women had been screened for cervical cancer under the national programme for prevention and control of non-communicable diseases, with 93,062 diagnoses reported.

Star Health said it conducted community health camps during H1 FY27, including initiatives focused on cancer screening and preventive healthcare, to improve awareness and encourage engagement with healthcare services.

Amitabh Jain, Whole-time Director and Chief Operating Officer, Star Health and Allied Insurance, said early detection must be accompanied by access to treatment and financial protection. He emphasised that financial preparedness should support the treatment journey rather than remain an afterthought following diagnosis.

Prof. Dr S. Rajasundaram, Surgical Oncologist, said cancer treatment often involves multiple stages, including chemotherapy, radiation, surgery and long-term monitoring. Financial constraints can lead families to postpone or discontinue treatment, potentially affecting clinical outcomes.

He highlighted health insurance as an important financial cushion that can help families access prescribed treatments and maintain continuity of care. The company said its focus remains on strengthening financial protection and encouraging preventive healthcare awareness, particularly among women.

data.description:
Earnings season reaches peak intensity this week as 142 companies report quarterly results, anchored by major releases across mega-cap technology, pharmaceuticals, energy, aerospace, and consumer goods.

Earnings Roundup:

Bottom Line: Out of the 142 companies reporting, 122 exceeded EPS expectations, while 13 fell short and 6 matched estimates. Notably, 111 firms posted year-over-year earnings growth.

Top Line: Out of the 142 companies reporting, 112 exceeded revenue expectations, while 28 fell below analyst estimates and 1 matched estimates. Notably, 112 firms posted year-over-year revenue growth.

Let’s take a look at some of the companies that reported earnings this week:

  • Apple : fell 1.90% post-earnings after reporting Q4 FY2026 revenue of $114.50B, up 6% Y/Y, beating the consensus estimate. Adjusted EPS of $2.10 beat the estimate by $0.11. Performance was bolstered by iPhone sales ($57.58B) and Mac revenue ($10.79B), offsetting slight headwinds in Greater China.
  • Palantir Technologies : fell 1.65% despite the double-beat and raised guidance. Reported Q3 2026 revenue of $2.31B, up 96% Y/Y, surpassing the $2.18B estimate. Adjusted EPS of $0.44 beat the $0.41 consensus. Growth was led by explosive adoption of its artificial intelligence platform, with US commercial revenue surging 148% Y/Y. The company raised its FY2026 revenue guidance to $8.530B–$8.534B.
  • Advanced Micro Devices : rose 1.01% post-earnings after reporting Q3 2026 revenue of $13.38B, up 45% Y/Y, topping the $13.06B consensus. Adjusted EPS of $2.09 beat the estimates by $0.15. Results were driven by record Data Center segment revenue of $8.55B (up 97% Y/Y). AMD guided Q4 revenue to approximately $17.0B.
  • Super Micro Computer : fell 5.70% despite delivering massive Q1 FY2027 beats, with revenue up 299.0% Y/Y to $19.95B (vs. $16.26B estimate) and non-GAAP EPS hitting $1.81 (vs. $1.23 estimate), driven by accelerating demand for its Total AI and IT Datacenter Solutions. Supermicro provided bullish guidance for Q2 FY2027, targeting revenue of $19.5B–$21.5B and non-GAAP EPS of $1.66–$1.90, both well ahead of consensus. Full-year FY2027 revenue is now expected between $72.0B and $82.0B.
  • Pfizer : fell 2.18% after reporting Q3 2026 revenue of $16.60B, up 7% Y/Y operational growth in non-COVID products, beating the $15.91B estimate. Adjusted EPS of $0.87 beat the $0.73 consensus. Strong demand for launched and acquired products ($3.8B, +32%) led Pfizer to raise its full-year 2026 revenue guidance to $62B–$64B.
  • Realty Income : fell 0.14% after reporting Q3 2026 revenue of $1.62B, surpassing the $1.43B consensus estimate. Adjusted EPS of $0.43 beat the $0.41 estimate, while Q3 AFFO per share came in at $1.12. Growth was driven by $2.6B in new investments during the quarter. Management reaffirmed its $10B annual investment target and slightly raised FY2026 AFFO guidance.
  • Qualcomm : fell 9.49% post-earnings despite beating Q4 estimates. Revenue declined 7.3% Y/Y to $10.44B (vs. $10.32B expected), while Non-GAAP EPS hit $2.17 (vs. $2.16 expected). Q1 guidance came in light, targeting revenue of $10.4B–$11.2B (vs. $10.55B estimate) and EPS of $2.15–$2.35 (vs. $2.29 estimate).
